title: Managing Certificates
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Managing Certificates and identify key concepts from the supplied syllabus.
Use an appropriate read-only check or controlled example to demonstrate managing certificates.

content.intro: This lesson introduces managing certificates as part of linux server administration. Begin with an observation you can safely repeat, then explain what the result tells you and what it does not prove.
content.why_it_matters: Plan repeatable server deployments for services, reverse proxies, TLS, shared services, and operational maintenance.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a Linux machine, WSL environment, or disposable virtual machine. Check the command with its local manual page before adapting it. The in-page example shows reference output only; it does not execute Bash/Linux commands on the CodeLeaf server. Commands and output formats may vary by distribution and installed utility version.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First, state what you expect from the example. Run it in the intended environment, capture standard output and any error message, and inspect the exit status where meaningful. Then connect the observation to this lesson: Managing Certificates. Do not infer more than the evidence supports.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake
content_blocks.text: A common mistake is to assume managing certificates behaves identically on every distribution, kernel, utility version, and administrative policy. Verify the installed tool and consult the matching manual before using the procedure elsewhere.

content_blocks.title: Safety and compatibility
content_blocks.text: Do not paste private-key material into lesson submissions or shell history. For commands that edit files, manage services, change network/firewall state, partition disks, change permissions recursively, or alter boot settings, use an isolated VM, take a snapshot/backup, review the exact target, and prepare a recovery path before acting.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the command is missing, check whether the required package is installed and which distribution you are using. If access is denied, do not immediately escalate to root; confirm the target path, identity, and required permission. If the result differs, capture the command, output, version, and environment so the issue can be reproduced.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember the core relationship: A production service needs repeatable configuration, restricted identity, validated deployment, logging, health checks, and a rollback path. The goal is to explain the observed result, test a boundary case, and record a limitation rather than memorize a command in isolation.

content.task: In an isolated Linux lab, investigate managing certificates. Use the guided example as a starting point, record the output/status, and test one boundary, failure, or distribution-specific case. Explain what you learned without changing a production system.
